She took a room above the chandler’s, where the window
faced the marsh. Reeds ran out to the horizon and a
single heron stood in them, patient as a fence post. By
evening she had drawn the room, the stair, and the
street as far as the pump, because drawing a place was
the only way she knew of arriving in it.

On the third day a boy came to the door and said he
could carry things. His name was Tomás and he was
eleven, or would be at Candlemas. His mother sold eels
from a barrow and called every stranger señora
regardless of evidence. Ada hired him for two pence a
day and a share of whatever the marsh turned out to
contain.
